children: Palm oil rises in early Asian trading, driven by gains in soybean oil on the Chicago Board of Trade as well as palm olein on the Dalian Commodity Exchange, says David Ng, a trader at Kuala Lumpur-based Iceberg X. He expects the uptrend to continue due to concerns about El Nino's impact on plam oil output. Ng expects prices to be supported at 4,900 ringgit a ton with resistance at 5,080 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for November delivery is up 32 ringgit at 4,936 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
